author: c2-sql-sme-critic (independent PostgreSQL SME critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; rechecked commit 02be5a14)

items.note: The keyed option is now WHERE credits = 3 ORDER BY fee DESC NULLS LAST, course_id; and the stem says "highest fee first and unpriced last". Simulator check on the page table: 101 (120.00) then 103 (NULL), as the 7.5 NULLS rule predicts. The distractors (course_id first; no tie-breaker; WHERE after ORDER BY) are explained correctly, and the static alternative and artifact.md match.

Verified in the simulator: ORDER BY 3, 1 DESC (Activity 2) and ORDER BY fee DESC NULLS LAST, 1 (Activity 3) now get an honest note that the practice check reads sort columns by name; neither note claims the order is unpromised or untied any more. Residual, low: an output alias used as a sort key (SELECT city AS town ... ORDER BY town) still gets "the order is not the one asked for", which is untrue for that query.

Partly fixed. The SQLCHK.explain branch now says "PostgreSQL has no operator for the two kinds of value on either side, for example a number and text. Check that both sides are the same kind of value", which is true and no longer calls a quoted literal text. Still open in the adapter (engine.js, recipe accepted): credits LIKE '3%' still prints "operator does not exist: integer ~~ text" where PostgreSQL reports the untyped literal as unknown, while LIMITS claims PostgreSQL's own ERROR wording. Server wording documented, not executed.

Raised in the f18bccaf recheck. Reverted at 94ab20b5: the EDITOR.check override is gone from controller.js and from the built artifact (verified in the git diff), so the adapter's limit messages again show as Not in this practice editor, which matches the LIMITS wording. Valid statements such as SELECT * FROM public.students or ORDER BY name COLLATE "C" are no longer labelled Error.
